desc:
Let M be the largest value in the whole array nums. Return the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays in which the value M occurs at least k times.

nums = [1, 3, 2, 3, 3], k = 2
M = 3; qualifying subarrays:
[1,3,2,3] [1,3,2,3,3] [3,2,3] [3,2,3,3] [2,3,3] [3,3]
result = 6
hints: Only the positions of the global maximum M matter. A subarray qualifies as soon as it covers k of them.
Extending a qualifying subarray in either direction keeps it qualifying. So for a fixed right end the valid starts form a prefix of the array.
Slide left as far as possible while the window still holds at least k copies of M. Then every start before the final left works, so add left to the answer for each right end.
editorial: First compute M. Walk the right end through the array and count copies of M in the window. While the window [left, right] contains at least k copies, drop nums[left] and advance left; when the loop stops, the window is no longer enough, but the starts 0..left-1 all produced windows that were. That is left valid subarrays ending at right.

This is the complement-style counterpart of the "at most" window: instead of counting subarrays that stay below a limit, we count those that reach it, and the valid starts form a prefix instead of a suffix. Each pointer only moves forward: O(n) time, O(1) space.
An equivalent view: answer = total subarrays - subarrays with fewer than k copies of M, and the latter is an "at most k-1" window count.
